value: Sep 9, 2026: people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that Kinetik was in the early stages of exploring alternatives and preparing a possible sale process that could begin within weeks; no final decision; in February the Financial Times reported an approach from Western Midstream that produced no deal.
Oxford Square Capital reported net asset value of $1.21 a share at Sept 30 (from $1.29) and declared monthly distributions of $0.015 a share for January to March 2027.

Icahn Enterprises declared a quarterly distribution of $0.50 per depositary unit, payable about Dec 23, 2026 to holders of record at the close of Nov 16, 2026, in cash or units at the holder's choice; its third-quarter net loss was $225 million.

Icahn Enterprises: a $0.50 distribution to holders of record on Nov 16, 2026; indicative net asset value about $3.5 billion at Sept 30; its stake in CVR Energy valued at $4.2 billion; $522 million of losses on refining hedges in its funds in the third quarter.

UroGen's Zusduri made $68.0 million in the third quarter, up 35% on the quarter; its next formulation UGN-103 is under FDA review for low-grade intermediate-risk bladder cancer (goal date June 14, 2027), and it plans a 2027 trial of UGN-103 as adjuvant therapy in newly diagnosed intermediate-risk disease.
On Nov 4 Molina rose 7.5% to $223.36 and Centene 8.9% after brokerages said the election result lowered policy risk for Medicaid-focused insurers and hospitals.
Genco's $1.05 per share dividend goes to holders of record on Nov 16, 2026.
Genco declared a record dividend of $1.05 per share for the third quarter, payable about Nov 23, 2026 to holders of record on Nov 16, 2026.

The Senate's defense bill carries three chip measures (congressional review of AI chip licenses, chip tracking abroad, allied limits on chipmaking tools); no vote has been taken; Nvidia's $108 billion third-quarter guidance excludes China data-center sales.

The House Speaker said on Nov 12 there is a developing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China; Nvidia billed $7.9 billion to customers in China including Hong Kong in the quarter to July 26, 8.2% of its total.

Truist cut Nvidia to Hold and its target to $174 from $346, saying the risks outweigh the valuation after the chief executive's resignation, including possible shipments to China; Craig-Hallum also cut it to Hold; William Blair and Oppenheimer upgraded AMD.

Bloomberg reported on Nov 12 that the Justice Department is investigating whether Super Micro servers were smuggled into China; Super Micro denies the reseller named was a customer; Dell fell 8% in the same session while Super Micro fell 3%.

Dell fell 8% as the AI server sell-off deepened after the Nvidia chief executive's resignation; it builds mostly around Nvidia hardware; its shares are down more than 35% in a month despite a $95 billion AI server backlog; it reports on Nov 24.

Rothschild & Co Redburn cut Broadcom to neutral and its target to $398 from $595, citing its reliance on OpenAI and Anthropic, which cannot yet pay their own way, and Broadcom's backstopping of customer financing.

Chaince Digital's quarterly report: about $34 million of cash and $14 million of short-term investments at Sept 30, a net loss of about $2.2 million over nine months, and conditions that at first raised substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern, which management says its plans and cash alleviate.
Inhibrx's third-quarter release: cash $199.5m on Sept 30; updated Ewing sarcoma data for ozekibart due at CTOS on Nov 19-20; ozekibart in chondrosarcoma under regulatory review

Espey's first fiscal quarter: sales $10.6 million against $9.1 million, net income $2.19 million against $2.17 million, new orders $2.6 million against $10.5 million a year earlier, backlog $126.7 million against $141.1 million.
Inhibrx's automatic shelf (S-3ASR) includes a $150m at-the-market sales agreement with Stifel and LifeSci Capital dated Nov 13, 2026; 14,759,126 shares outstanding; last sale $87.745 on Nov 12

AMD fell 9% Friday, giving back part of a ~30% week, with no news of its own; Marvell -5%, Intel -3%, Arm -5%; Nvidia -2% after HSBC cut it to Hold; the 10-year yield hit 5.17% after the wholesale inflation reading; AMD at about 35 times forward earnings after the drop

After Friday's close the federal Medicaid agency offered states an optional transition period to June 30, 2027 for the new Medicaid work rules, during which states will not deny or drop otherwise eligible people solely for failing them; Centene rose 2.5% and Molina 2.6% in extended trading.

Fortune: Super Micro says Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the center of the scandal around Nvidia's former chief, was never its customer; Singapore said it got only limited cooperation from Super Micro; US prosecutors are reportedly examining whether Super Micro hardware with Nvidia GPUs was smuggled to China; no one has been charged
Simply Wall St: Modine is reported to be in acquisition talks with Samsung Electronics over its data center cooling division, which has a sizeable order backlog

Financial Times: Trump Media faces a Nov 30 deadline to repay up to $1 billion of convertible bonds that convert at $34.72 against a share price of $4.64; it may have to sell assets including crypto holdings worth about $1.36 billion at the end of the third quarter, or borrow at high cost; it lost $234 million in nine months.

MSCI will delete Strategy from its equity indexes at month-end under new rules for companies that mostly hold financial assets; JPMorgan estimates up to $8.8 billion of outflows if other index providers follow, against Strategy's earlier estimate of about $2.8 billion; Strategy's $5.07 billion of dollar assets cover 3.4 years of dividends and interest.

AI-linked stocks extended losses before the open on concern about the sector's growth and financing risks: Nvidia -1.8% ahead of Tuesday's results, AMD -4%, Micron -5%, Sandisk -5.3%, Western Digital -4.4%, CoreWeave -4.7% with peers IREN and Nebius; Capital.com called Nvidia the biggest immediate source of uncertainty.

AMD and Broadcom fell before the open in a wider chip sell-off; Commerzbank Research called the fallout from the leadership turmoil at Nvidia the dominant driver of risk sentiment, with investors moving into rival chip makers and then unwinding those positions too; reports that the former chief may return have not lifted Nvidia; AMD and Broadcom were still about 13% higher over five sessions and the Philadelphia chip index about 7%.

The FDA's complete response letter says ivonescimab's application cannot be approved in its present form: effectiveness is not established without a statistically significant improvement in overall survival; the HARMONi trial met its progression-free survival goal and showed a survival trend short of significance (hazard ratio 0.76 in a later analysis).

Crypto stocks fell before the open as bitcoin traded near $64,600, close to a three-month low, on expectations of a Fed rate rise in December (some traders pricing a half-point move) and uncertainty over crypto rules; Strategy fell more than 7%, Circle 7.6%, Coinbase 6.4%.
Clearwater Paper named a new finance chief and said repairs at its Augusta mill after disruptions in late September and October are largely complete, with the mill returning to normal operations.

Aramark's outlook for fiscal 2027: organic revenue growth of 9% to 10%, adjusted operating income growth of 15% to 19% and adjusted earnings per share growth of 20% to 25%; a new $1 billion buyback and a 17% higher dividend; incentive pay tied to outperformance took $0.07 off fourth-quarter earnings per share.

In the week of Nov 9-15 Strategy sold 2,087,040 common shares for $244.7 million net: $206.3 million went to buying back its STRC preferred stock, $33.4 million to 485 bitcoin at $68,887 each and $5.0 million to cash; it holds 850,849 bitcoin at an average cost of $75,452.

CG Oncology's Phase 3 trial PIVOT-006 met its main goal: cretostimogene cut the risk of recurrence by 68% (hazard ratio 0.32, 95% interval 0.23-0.45, p<0.0001) in intermediate-risk and high-grade Ta bladder cancer with no grade 3 or higher treatment-related side effects; about 50,000 patients have no approved treatment of this kind; a second FDA application is planned for the second quarter of 2027.

Dow Jones: AI stocks led a broader sell-off before Nvidia's results on Tuesday and the pricing of Anthropic's offering; Asian technology indexes closed sharply lower; XTB's strategist ties the selling to fears that Republicans and Democrats will combine to tighten limits on chips that may go to China, cutting spending on chips and data centers; the 10-year yield fell to about 5.13%; Brent fell 1% to below $95.

The Nasdaq opened 1.5% lower and the S&P 500 about 1%; Nvidia lost 13% last week; the weakness reached AI infrastructure (CoreWeave -5.2%, Nebius -8%, IREN, Applied Digital, Core Scientific); Anthropic is reported to target a valuation of about $1.4 trillion with shares priced between $70 and $78; a Financial Times report says Nvidia's former chief is considering a return.

Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim rule on Monday requiring licenses to export, re-export or transfer advanced AI chips to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, to stop restricted countries reaching US chips by renting computing in third-country data centers.

After the FDA's letter Barclays cut its Summit target to $18 from $20 (Equal Weight) and Citi to $42 from $43 (Buy), Jefferies kept Buy at $30; Barclays sees limited direct effect on value but what seems a higher FDA bar for the lung cancer program.
Molina rose just over 8% on Monday morning to $226.47 as managed-care peers also gained: Centene just over 5%, Elevance almost 4%; the report gives no cause.

Trump Media fell 12% to $4.10 ahead of a $976.8 million convertible-note obligation with a near-term demand feature and a shareholder vote on its TAE merger; it is down 43% in a month; Rumble fell almost as hard as speculative and AI-linked stocks sold off, with funding needs and softer guidance weighing on it.

Red Cat withdrew its full-year 2026 revenue target: funding and contract awards have come more slowly than expected and the outcome of the Drone Dominance program's Gauntlet II removed an expected contributor; third-quarter revenue $11.8 million (+22%), nine months $47.4 million; cash $242.7 million.
Icahn Enterprises closed at $3.60 on Monday, down 15.09%, after its units went ex-distribution for the $0.50 distribution to holders of record on Nov 16.

Around noon the Dow -1.4%, S&P 500 -1.3%, Nasdaq -1.6%; Nvidia fell over 3% early and pared losses after the Wall Street Journal published a statement from its former chief that he would return as chief executive if the board decided it was in shareholders' interest; Disney and Home Depot beat estimates; homebuilder confidence at its lowest in over 14 years.
Futures about -0.4% before Nvidia's report and retail sales; analysts expect Nvidia revenue of about $109 billion; Nvidia closed Monday at $156.14 (-4.12%).
Spire lowered its fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings guidance to $5.05-$5.25 a share, introduced fiscal 2028 guidance of $6.10-$6.30, raised its long-term growth target to 6%-8% and its dividend by 4.8%.

Sellas' Phase 3 REGAL trial of its vaccine galinpepimut-S in acute myeloid leukemia met its main goal: 41% lower risk of death (hazard ratio 0.59, two-sided p 0.035), median survival 24.0 months against 14.7 with the best available treatment; it plans to meet the FDA and prepare an application.

Nvidia's guidance was $108 billion plus or minus 2% with a 74% gross margin; Visible Alpha expects $109.3 billion and data-center revenue of about $101.8 billion; Anthropic plans to list on Nov 19; Red Cat fell over 30% before the open after withdrawing its 2026 revenue guidance.

By 5:23am ET S&P 500 E-minis were -0.34%; Nvidia slipped 0.4% before its results; CNBC reported Nvidia told customers it would stop selling chips to data-center operators that rent more than half their GPUs to Chinese companies; Intel fell over 3% after Nvidia cut its stake in Intel in a portfolio reshuffle (also Nokia and Synopsys, while adding SpaceX); Home Depot named its finance chief as next chief executive and raised its sales outlook to the top of its range.

Stocks reversed from overnight gains to trade lower before Nvidia's results and Anthropic's listing; Bank of America's November survey shows investors cut their tech overweight by the most since 2006 and 52% expect a major AI hyperscaler to announce a capex cut within six months (30% in October); October retail sales +0.2% as expected, industrial output -0.4%; per CNBC, Nvidia will halt sales to data centers renting over 50% of their GPUs to Chinese firms and set up a board committee on national security and export compliance; Nvidia's board said late Monday it is not considering reinstating its former chief; Anthropic may price above its $70-$78 range.

Salesforce fell 9% with no news of its own as seat-priced software slid a day before Anthropic's offering prices; the article argues funds are selling software to make room for an offering that could raise up to about $64 billion, notes the software ETF fell 7% around SpaceX's June listing while the Nasdaq 100 rose 3%, and puts Salesforce's forward P/E near 15 against a five-year average of 27.

The S&P 500 software and services index fell 7.1% to its lowest in over three months: Salesforce -9.8%, ServiceNow -7.2%, MongoDB -7.3%, Intuit -6.8%, Okta -4.9%, Adobe -4.1%; a portfolio manager calls it risk reduction in higher-valued stocks before Nvidia's results.

Omeros fell about 21% at midday, its worst day since May 2025: the European Medicines Agency's committee gave a negative opinion on its drug in October after re-examination, the company said it is shifting its near-term regulatory strategy outside the EU and closing its EU compassionate-use program to new patients, and gave no outlook despite rising US sales.
AECOM rose over 12% after fourth-quarter results and fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.15-$6.35, 4.4% above consensus at the midpoint (UBS).
BILL rose about 8% after the Financial Times reported TPG is nearing a deal to take it private at a premium to its $4.8 billion market value; TPG declined to comment and talks could still fail.

The federal Medicare agency proposed the CRUSH anti-fraud rule: risk-adjustment audits of Medicare Advantage plans without a fee-for-service adjuster, with findings extrapolated from payment year 2018; it estimates recovering about $9 billion per payment year and HHS about $90 billion over 2027-2036; comments are due Jan 19, 2027.

Nvidia's third quarter: revenue $115.8 billion (+103% on the year, +20% on the quarter), data-center revenue $107.6 billion (+110%), GAAP gross margin 74.8%; fourth-quarter outlook $130.0 billion plus or minus 3% with no China data-center compute revenue assumed and gross margin 71%-72%; Vera Rubin NVL72 has shipped.

Ardent Health priced a secondary offering of 8,000,000 shares (7,136,719 from an affiliate of Equity Group Investments, 863,281 from an affiliate of Ventas) at $14.50, with a 1,200,000-share option; the company will buy back 1,500,000 of them from the underwriters at their price, from cash; it sells no shares and receives nothing.

Revenue and adjusted EPS ($2.68) beat LSEG estimates of $109.10 billion and $2.48; the $130 billion outlook beat a $125.1 billion average; the interim chief raised the fiscal 2028 growth outlook to about 75% from 70%; the board's chair said it does not intend to reinstate the former chief; revenue from customers headquartered in China including Hong Kong was $11.1 billion; shares about +3.6% after hours at 5:48pm ET.

Ecovyst's board appointed a director as interim chief executive effective November 17, replacing the chief executive, who is departing and will consult until February 5, 2027; no reason given; fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 guidance of November 5 reaffirmed; a search for a permanent chief has begun.

UnitedHealth fell 5.42% to $389.68 on Nov 17 after CMS's Nov 16 CRUSH proposal: Medicare Advantage audits extrapolated from samples back to payment year 2018, the fee-for-service adjuster dropped, about $9 billion a payment year recovered industrywide; comments due Jan 19, 2027; a 2023 rule with the same features was vacated in Sept 2025 and is on appeal at the Fifth Circuit; UnitedHealth has not quantified its exposure.
Hyster-Yale amended its credit agreement to permit certain financing transactions and announced a proposed private offering of $125 million of convertible senior notes due 2031.

BellRing's fourth quarter: net sales $692.0 million (+7%), net earnings $35.6 million, adjusted EBITDA $66.4 million after a $16 million inventory charge; fiscal 2026 sales $2,398.4 million and adjusted EBITDA $288.8 million after $37 million of inventory headwinds; fiscal 2027 outlook: sales $2.32-$2.42 billion and adjusted EBITDA $310-$350 million.
Cal-Maine: avian influenza at a Florida facility; about 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 pullets, 2.7% of its flock, will be depopulated; production there has stopped.

TJX third quarter: comparable sales +4% (above plan), Marmaxx +2%; sales $16.0 billion (+6%); EPS $1.39, adjusted $1.34 (+5%) excluding a $0.05 net tariff-refund benefit; adjusted gross margin -0.5 point on freight and fuel; the chief executive expects sales momentum to accelerate through the holidays.

Newmont -5.13% to $105.56 at 9:40 ET as December gold fell to about $3,767.60, tied by Yahoo Finance to a 96.7% FedWatch probability of a Fed rate increase; at that price its margin over a $1,520 cost guide is about $2,248 an ounce, about 20% less than at its third-quarter realized price of $4,317.

Red Robin's third quarter: comparable restaurant revenue +3.9% (traffic -1.7%, check +5.6%), adjusted EBITDA $7.3 million; about $100 million borrowed and total liquidity of about $29.5 million ($23.8 million cash); fourth-quarter outlook: comparable revenue about +2.75%, adjusted EBITDA about $6.0 million, updated for refranchising.

Magnera's fourth quarter: net sales $851 million, operating loss $90 million including $106 million of impairments, adjusted EBITDA +8% on a better price-cost spread; volumes down 4%; fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA $378 million.

StoneX's fourth quarter: diluted EPS $0.66 against a $0.81 consensus; net operating revenues $655.2 million (+12%); net income $84.2 million (-2%); shares -6.2% after hours Wednesday; fiscal-year net income a record $525.4 million.
Sellas priced 11,538,462 new shares at $13.00 in an underwritten public offering, all sold by the company, about $150 million gross.

Liquidity Services' fiscal fourth quarter: GMV $404.0 million against $404.5 million a year earlier, revenue $106.4 million (-10%) with a shift to consignment, GAAP net income $11.9 million (+52%); fiscal 2027 GMV expected to exceed $2 billion after the Invaluable acquisition.

Valvoline's fiscal 2026: sales $2.1 billion (+21%), system-wide same-store sales +7.9%, adjusted EBITDA $557 million (+19%), adjusted EPS $1.76 (+11%); it expects another year of strong growth in fiscal 2027.

Walmart's quarter: revenue $188.8 billion (+5.2%, 0.8% above consensus), adjusted EPS $0.65 (consensus $0.64), same-store sales +2.9% (4.4% a year earlier), operating margin 4.1% flat; full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised 1.1% to $2.87 at the midpoint.

Williams-Sonoma's third quarter: comparable brand revenue +5.1%, non-GAAP EPS $2.19 (+11.7%); gross margin +150 basis points, of which 140 from IEEPA tariff refunds, with higher oil prices costing 50 in supply chain; fiscal 2026 guidance reiterated, not raised.
Savara: the FDA will not meet the Nov 22, 2026 PDUFA date for its molgramostim BLA in autoimmune PAP; the review continues and no revised action date has been given.

Vertex: the FDA told it on Nov 24 that it extends the target date for its decision on povetacicept in IgA nephropathy by up to three months, from Nov 30, 2026 to no later than Feb 28, 2027; the agency asked for information late in the review and classed Vertex's reply as a major amendment; Vertex says it is confident in the data.

Vertex fell after hours on the FDA's delay; Vera Therapeutics, whose TRUTAKNA won accelerated approval in July 2026 for the same kidney disease, rose more than 17% after hours as head-to-head competition is put off.

Vera closed at $29.50 on Wednesday and traded at $34.43 by 7:59 p.m. ET (+16.72%); Vertex fell 6.95% after hours to $524.94 from $564.12. Trutakna won accelerated approval on July 7, 2026 and brought in $10.3 million in its first partial quarter, about half of it pharmacies building stock; Vera lost $93.7 million in the third quarter and had $384.0 million of cash and securities at September 30, about $459 million after a $75 million debt draw. Vertex's drug is dosed once every four weeks against Trutakna's weekly injection. Vertex did not say what the FDA asked for; its own warning says approval may not come by the new date or at all. Vera's Wednesday close was 41.75% below its close of December 31, 2025.

Zacks: the FDA accepted Vertex's application for povetacicept in June 2026; the drug came with the purchase of Alpine in 2024; other drugs for the same kidney disease are Novartis's Fabhalta, Travere's Filspari and Calliditas's Tarpeyo. The page's price strip showed Vertex -7.23%, Vera +18.77%, Travere +0.81% and Novartis +0.60%. Vertex is up 24.4% this year against 11.9% for its industry.

Bloomberg News reported that Targa Resources is in talks to buy Kinetik and that a deal could come as soon as next week; nothing is signed and no price is reported. Kinetik closed at $54.70 on Wednesday and traded at $58.85 at 7:56 p.m. ET (+7.59%), just under its 52-week high of $58.90; Targa closed at $285.53 and traded at $280.48 (-1.77%). Blackstone holds about 48% of Kinetik and I Squared Capital about 19%. Kinetik is valued at about $9 billion against Targa's $61.24 billion; Kinetik owes $3.95 billion and Targa $19.8 billion. Kinetik was reported to weigh a sale in February and in September. On Nov 5 its management called asset prices less attractive than building its own plants. Kinetik is up 62% this year.
